title: The two middle exactness assertions of Jacobi–Zariski
statement: Let $R\to S\to T$ be homomorphisms of commutative rings, with compatible algebra structures. Let $H_1(L_{T/R})$ and $H_1(L_{T/S})$ be the first homologies of the canonical naive cotangent complexes [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map], and let $v:H_1(L_{T/R})\to H_1(L_{T/S})$ be the map changing coefficients in the canonical presentations $R[T]\to S[T]$ [lem-weil-pbc-nl-presentation-h1-functoriality]. Let $\Omega$ and $\mathrm d$ be the universal differentials [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials]. Let $\partial:H_1(L_{T/S})\to T\otimes_S\Omega_{S/R}$ be the canonical Jacobi–Zariski connecting map: on a cycle represented by $g=\sum_\alpha s_\alpha[t]^\alpha$ in the kernel of $S[T]\to T$, it sends its class to $\sum_\alpha \operatorname{ev}([t]^\alpha)\otimes\mathrm d s_\alpha$. Let $w:T\otimes_S\Omega_{S/R}\to\Omega_{T/R}$ send $t\otimes\mathrm ds$ to $t\,\mathrm d(\overline s)$. Then $\ker\partial=\operatorname{im}v$ and $\ker w=\operatorname{im}\partial$.

proof.text: Apply Mathlib Algebra.H1Cotangent.exact_map_δ and Algebra.H1Cotangent.exact_δ_mapBaseChange, respectively, to the given tower. These have exactly the canonical coefficient-change map, the coefficient-derivative connecting map, and the base-changed universal differential map specified in the statement. One already-proved Mathlib theorem supplies each assertion; no left term, Tor assertion, or auxiliary presentation comparison is needed.
